turns.prompt_text: Where can I buy a rug? Can I make a rug? I need a very large one, around 9' by 9'
turns.response_html:
Finding a 9' x 9' square rug can be a bit of a challenge since most standard rugs are rectangular (like 8' x 10' or 9' x 12'). However, you can find them through specialized retailers or even make one yourself using a few different DIY methods.

Where to Buy 9' x 9' Square Rugs

While many physical stores focus on standard rectangles, several online retailers carry a wide variety of 9' x 9' square options. Brands like Safavieh and Jonathan Y offer many styles in this specific size, ranging from natural fibers to plush shags.

  • Large Retailers: Websites like Walmart, The Home Depot, and Bed Bath & Beyond have extensive "9x9 square" filters.
  • Specialty Rug Shops: Rugs Direct and Joss & Main often carry more curated or premium square designs.
  • Custom/Handmade: Etsy is an excellent source for handmade 9' x 9' rugs, often allowing for custom colors or patterns.

Can You Make a 9' x 9' Rug?

Yes, you can certainly make a rug of this size, though it is a significant undertaking. At 81 square feet, a 9' x 9' rug requires a large workspace and a fair amount of materials. Here are the most common DIY methods:

  • Canvas Drop Cloth Rug: This is the most beginner-friendly method. You can buy a large 12' x 15' heavy-duty canvas drop cloth, cut and hem it to 9' x 9' using fusible web tape or a sewing machine, and then paint it with fabric paint.
  • Fabric & Drop Cloth Sandwich: For a softer, "washable" feel, you can sew two pieces of 54" wide home decor fabric together to create a 9' width, then sew it to a canvas backing like a giant pillowcase.
  • Rug Tufting: This involves using a tufting gun to shoot yarn through a backing cloth stretched on a frame. To make a 9' x 9' rug, you would need to build a massive 10' x 10' wooden frame, which requires substantial space.
  • Rag Rug Weaving: You can build a large frame loom out of 2x2 lumber and weave fabric strips through warp threads. While traditional and sturdy, weaving a 9' x 9' section is very time-consuming.

Pro Tip: If you choose a DIY route for such a large rug, be sure to apply caulk or rug tape to the bottom once finished to prevent it from sliding on hard floors.

turns.prompt_text: I'm looking for low cost relative to how much rug, I could even stitch many low-cost rugs together if that is more affordable than one large rug, the exact size does not matter, it just needs to cover a lot of space
turns.response_html:
When covering a very large space on a budget, you typically have three main paths: buying a single oversized machine-made rug, stitching multiple smaller rugs together, or purchasing carpet remnants.

Comparing Your Options

While stitching smaller rugs can be cheaper upfront, a single large machine-made rug is often the most cost-effective per square foot because it avoids the labor and extra material (like seams and double edges) of multiple smaller pieces.

MethodEstimated Cost (approx. 9' x 9')Best ForPros
Single Large Rug$30 – $100High-traffic living areasMost cohesive look; no seams to trip on.
Stitched Rugs$40 – $80Unique or bohemian stylesHighly customizable; can use mismatched patterns.
Carpet Remnants$20 – $60Max coverage for least costCheapest option; very durable.

Top Low-Cost Large Rugs

If you prefer a single piece, clearance sections and synthetic materials like polypropylene offer the best value. These rugs are often under $100 even for 9' x 12' sizes.

  • Boho Floral Medallion Area Rug: At 9' x 12', this is one of the most affordable ways to cover a large space. It is machine-washable and features a non-slip backing, which is rare for such a large size.
  • Edx Collection Decorative Rug: This 9' x 12' rug uses a low-pile construction that is easy to clean and fits under most doors.
  • Nuloom Daniela Jute Area Rug: If you prefer a natural look, jute is a classic budget choice. It's durable and provides a thick, knotted texture that covers floor imperfections well.

How to Stitch Rugs Together

If you find several 3' x 5' or 5' x 7' rugs on deep clearance, you can combine them into one large piece.

  1. Select Flat-Weave Rugs: Avoid "shag" or thick rugs, as the seams will be very bulky. Thin woven or cotton rugs work best.
  2. Use Carpet Seaming Tape: For a no-sew option, lay the rugs face down and apply heavy-duty fiberglass carpet tape along the seam.
  3. Woven Tie Method: If you have hand-woven rugs, you can unpick the end stitches and tie the warp threads (the long vertical strings) of two rugs together for a nearly invisible seam.
  4. Zig-Zag Stitch: If you have a heavy-duty sewing machine, you can butt the edges together and use a wide zig-zag stitch to join them.

Pro-Tip: The "Remnant" Secret

The absolute cheapest way to get a 9' x 9' "rug" is to visit a local flooring or carpet store and ask for remnants. These are leftover pieces from wall-to-wall carpet installations. You can often get a high-quality piece of carpet for a fraction of the price of an area rug. Many stores will even "bind" (sew) the edges for a small fee so it doesn't fray.

turns.prompt_text: Where could I find a discount rug? Dollar stores?
turns.response_html:
While dollar stores like Dollar General or Dollar Tree do sell rugs, they are typically much smaller accent rugs (around 1.5' x 2') rather than the large area rugs you're looking for. However, you can find surprisingly affordable large rugs at major retailers and discount shops, often for under $50 even for sizes like 8' x 10'.

Best Places for Discount Large Rugs

For the most coverage at the lowest price, Walmart and TikTok Shop currently offer some of the most aggressive "rollback" or "clearance" pricing for large synthetic rugs.

  • Walmart (Ames): Local stores on S Duff Ave and Grand Ave often have large 8' x 10' rugs in their home sections, with some recent "Rollback" prices starting as low as $13.00 for certain low-pile models.
  • TikTok Shop: This has become a popular spot for extremely low-priced, machine-washable area rugs. Prices for 8' x 10' sizes can frequently be found between $19 and $35.
  • Discount Home Stores: In the Ames area, Menards and Hobby Lobby are reliable options for finding rugs on sale. Menards often has "Value After Rebate" deals that significantly lower the final price.

Top Budget-Friendly Large Rugs

The following options offer the most square footage for the lowest cost, with some being even larger than your 9' x 9' target.

  • DEXI Area Rug: This 8' x 10' washable rug features a vintage floral design and a non-slip backing, making it practical for high-traffic areas.
  • Large Shaggy Fuzzy Rug: A very affordable 8' x 10' plush option that provides a soft, thick feel for less than $20.
  • Washable Stripe Area Rug: A modern, neutral-toned 8' x 10' rug that is lightweight and easy to clean in a standard washing machine.

Dollar Store Rug Strategy

If you want to use dollar store rugs to cover a large space, you would need to buy several and join them.

  • Dollar General carries "Comfort Bay" rugs that are occasionally available in larger 5' x 7' sizes for a higher price point than their standard $1 items.
  • Five Below is another great option; they often have 4' x 6' rugs for around $5.55, which could be stitched together more easily than dozens of tiny doormats.

Local Ames Discount Tips

Since you're in Ames, I recommend checking the clearance aisles at the Walmart Supercenter on South Duff first. They frequently mark down area rugs that were floor models or have slightly damaged packaging. Additionally, The Furniture Mart on SE 5th St sometimes has rug remnants or floor-model rugs at a significant discount.
